key_insight: A 90° chirality-induced rotation maps classical 2D Stokes fluid mechanics into a complete chiral hydrodynamic theory with paired mechanical and spin responses.
engineering_relevance: The framework gives closed-form predictions for cavity flows and base states in active chiral suspensions, useful for designing and interpreting microfluidic and granular experiments.
method: Derived the full stress tensor and spin flux from angular-momentum conservation without assuming stress symmetry.
Used irreducible decomposition to pair classical channels with chiral counterparts (pressure, bulk/shear viscosities, spin-flux gradients).
Solved the chiral Stokes cavity in circular geometry analytically and square geometry numerically, governed by one dimensionless control group.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports closed-form circular solutions, numerical square-domain results, and direct quantitative comparison with experiments on air-fluidised chiral disks.
watch_item: The theory’s predictions depend on idealized 2D assumptions and a single control parameter, so real systems may require careful calibration of spin, boundary, and confinement effects.
paper_title: Steady base states in a two-dimensional chiral fluid. The chiral Stokes cavity
